3._section_summary: This section describes the statistical testing of a hypothesized structural model with 249 participants using Mplus software. The analysis examined relationships among restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages, attachment anxiety/avoidance, perfectionism dimensions, body appreciation, depressive symptoms, and intuitive eating, with BMI controlled as a covariate. The final model demonstrated good fit and revealed that body appreciation was predicted by multiple factors and in turn predicted intuitive eating, with substantial variance explained across model variables.

3._section_summary: This conclusion section summarizes findings from a study examining interpersonal and intrapersonal links to body appreciation and its connection to intuitive eating among college women. Body appreciation served as a central mediator between caregiver eating messages, attachment anxiety, perfectionism, and intuitive eating, suggesting it is an important clinical intervention target. The study found that body appreciation did not predict depressive symptoms, indicating it is distinct from negative body image.
